exposure: regional cerebrovascular reserve on single-photon emission computed tomography
cohort: The study participants were patients with moyamoya disease who gave birth.
finding: Patients with severely reduced regional cerebrovascular reserve and frequent transient ischemic attacks (TIAs) before pregnancy may experience neurologic deterioration during pregnancy, delivery, and puerperium, while surgical revascularization before pregnancy may decrease this deterioration.
followup_time: Throughout pregnancy, delivery, and puerperium (including recovery to prepregnancy levels after puerperium)
